questions.question: What is the shortest correct way to initialize an empty JSON object in ObjectScript?

options.text: SET obj = ##class(%DynamicObject).%New()
SET obj = {}
SET obj = []
SET obj = %New(%DynamicObject)

questions.explanation: `{}` is the literal constructor for an empty %DynamicObject. It is shorter than calling ##class(%DynamicObject).%New().

questions.question: Which ObjectScript statement correctly creates a JSON object using runtime values inside a literal constructor?

options.text: SET obj = {"name":person.Name,"active":person.Active}
SET obj = {"name":(person.Name),"active":(person.Active)}
SET obj = {name=(person.Name),active=(person.Active)}
SET obj = {"name"=(person.Name),"active"=(person.Active)}

questions.explanation: Inside a JSON literal constructor, ObjectScript runtime expressions must be wrapped in parentheses, for example {"name":(person.Name)}.

questions.question: Which GET request lets you identify the routes available for the /rest/bookinventory service at ABCbookstore.com using the IRIS REST management API?

options.text: GET http://ABCbookstore.com:52773/rest/bookinventory/routes
GET http://ABCbookstore.com:52773/api/mgmnt/v1/USER/spec/bookinventory
GET http://ABCbookstore.com:8001/services/rest%2Fbookinventory/routes
GET http://ABCbookstore.com:52773/csp/sys/api/bookinventory

questions.explanation: The IRIS REST management endpoint that returns the OpenAPI/Swagger spec is GET /api/mgmnt/v1/<namespace>/spec/<application>. From that spec, you can identify the available routes.

questions.question: What does GET /api/mgmnt/v1/<namespace>/spec/<application> return?

options.text: Only the web application path prefix
A list of globals used by the REST service
A Swagger / OpenAPI 2.0 specification for the REST application
A compiled dispatch class source listing

questions.explanation: According to the IRIS REST reference, this endpoint returns the Swagger (OpenAPI 2.0) specification for the given REST application.

questions.question: Which statements about REST ClassMethods in IRIS are correct? (select all that apply)

options.text: The method should RETURN $$$OK even when the HTTP status is 404 or 400
HTTP status is set through %response.Status
The request body is typically read from %request.Content
The method should RETURN the HTTP numeric code instead of $$$OK
A Web Application must be configured before the Dispatch Class can receive HTTP requests

questions.explanation: A, B, C, and E are all core REST patterns in IRIS. The return value is $$$OK for ObjectScript execution status; the HTTP status code is controlled separately through %response.Status.

questions.question: Which is the correct way to handle invalid JSON when using dynamic entities in ObjectScript?

options.text: Call %FromJSON() and only check $$$ISERR(sc) afterward
Wrap %FromJSON() in TRY/CATCH because invalid JSON can throw an exception
Use DO {}.%FromJSON(json) because DO suppresses parse errors
Always ignore parse failures and default to an empty object

questions.explanation: %FromJSON() on dynamic entities can throw an exception for invalid JSON, so the correct pattern is TRY/CATCH around the parse operation.

questions.question: In a REST endpoint that parses a request body into a dynamic object, which snippet is most correct for invalid JSON handling?

options.text: SET body = {}.%FromJSON(%request.Content.Read())
SET sc = {}.%FromJSON(%request.Content.Read()) IF $$$ISERR(sc) { SET %response.Status = "400 Bad Request" }
TRY { SET body = {}.%FromJSON(%request.Content.Read()) } CATCH ex { SET %response.Status = "400 Bad Request" WRITE {"error":"Invalid JSON","detail":(ex.DisplayString())}.%ToJSON() RETURN $$$OK }
SET %response.Status = "400 Bad Request" SET body = {}

questions.explanation: This is the safest REST pattern: catch exceptions from %FromJSON(), set an HTTP 400 response, write an error payload, and still RETURN $$$OK from the ClassMethod.

questions.question: Which statements about %FromJSON() and dynamic entities are correct? (select all that apply)

options.text: {}.%FromJSON(jsonString) can parse JSON into a dynamic object
Invalid JSON may raise an exception that should be handled with TRY/CATCH
%FromJSON() automatically converts all parse errors into $$$OK / $$$ERROR values only
If your public method returns %Status, you can catch the exception and convert it into an error status
In REST code, invalid JSON is a good reason to return HTTP 400 Bad Request

questions.explanation: A, B, D, and E are correct. %FromJSON() is used to parse JSON into dynamic entities, invalid JSON may throw, and callers often convert errors into %Status or HTTP 400 responses.

questions.question: Which statement best describes the application parameter in GET /api/mgmnt/v1/<namespace>/spec/<application>?

options.text: It must always be the exact web application path, such as /rest/bookinventory
It is the fully qualified package name that contains the REST service class
It is the IAM service identifier
It is the CSP physical directory on disk

questions.explanation: The REST reference defines application as the fully qualified name of the package that contains the REST service class. It is not simply the visible web application path.

questions.question: A method catches an exception from %FromJSON() and wants to continue using standard ObjectScript error flow. What is the best next step?

options.text: Return an error %Status such as $$$ERROR(...)
Return 0
QUIT without returning anything
Overwrite the exception object with {} and retry automatically

questions.explanation: If the method contract uses %Status, the idiomatic pattern is to catch the exception and return an error %Status, preserving normal IRIS error handling.
